title: How to Stick with Good Habits Every Day
coreMove: Build a visible streak you refuse to break twice, using a tracker that proves the identity to yourself

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice nurse marking an X on a wall calendar after each twelve-hour shift she journals about a single patient
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinician trying to keep a reflective practice alive across brutal weeks
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the practice survives the first week she forgets, or dies the way three previous attempts did
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the satisfaction of marking the X is shown as the reward that closes the loop, not the journaling itself

exampleSpecs.domain: a freight dispatcher who tracks daily back stretches on a paper card taped inside his locker after a herniated disc scare
exampleSpecs.audience: a shift worker in his fifties whose body is the asset
exampleSpecs.stakes: a second injury that would end his ability to work the dock
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the tracker is shown moving the cue, the response, and the reward into one physical object he passes every morning

exampleSpecs.domain: a violin teacher who misses her morning practice on a Tuesday because of a dentist appointment and has to decide whether Wednesday counts as a fresh start or a second miss
exampleSpecs.audience: a working musician whose income depends on her own playing not slipping
exampleSpecs.stakes: the unraveling of a 142-day practice streak that has changed how she introduces herself
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she names the rule out loud — never miss twice — and treats Wednesday as the load-bearing day, not Thursday

exampleSpecs.domain: a single father of a seven-year-old trying to hold a nightly ten-minute reading habit with his daughter through a custody-week schedule
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent whose habit lives inside someone else's calendar
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether his daughter learns that reading together is what they do, or what they sometimes do
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he designs a tracker the daughter fills in, so the measurement itself becomes the ritual that pulls them both in

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional sales manager who notices he has started optimizing for the tracker — logging short, junk workouts just to keep the chain — instead of for the fitness the tracker was meant to prove
exampleSpecs.audience: a goal-driven professional prone to gaming any metric put in front of him
exampleSpecs.stakes: the habit becomes theater while the underlying identity quietly erodes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he separates the measure from the thing measured, and rewrites the rule so a logged session has to meet a floor before it counts

exampleSpecs.domain: a recovering gambler choosing whether to tell his sponsor about a single missed check-in call, or quietly skip it and protect the streak number
exampleSpecs.audience: someone whose recovery depends on honesty more than on appearances
exampleSpecs.stakes: the difference between a streak that reflects reality and a streak that hides a relapse in progress
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the tracker is reframed as a mirror, not a trophy — useful only to the extent it tells the truth
